chapter: Becoming a musician: ukulele, clarinet and the Boozaire Kings
title: The Lyric Theatre, its Chinese doorman and the five-dollar prize
summary: The Lyric was a big Black theatre; the doorman threatened tenor Charlie Henderson, and the band won five dollars. End of Tape 1 side B.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: [LAUGHS] Yeah, that was at that theatre... The Lyric Theatre? What was the name again?
The Lyric Theatre was like the...
Like the Apollo, sort of, huh?
Yeah. Well, it was bigger than the Apollo. Actually it was bigger.

The Lyric. We went on there for the Amateur Hour. The stage doorman was Chinese. And I remember he had a fight with a cat named Charlie, a one-legged guy who sang like a tenor -- Charlie Henderson. You might have seen him in Chicago. He came out with a white full-dress suit and one leg. It was a cork leg, you couldn't see it. But he sang tenor. They got in an argument. They had an argument backstage about some woman. And the Chinese threatened to kill him and all that shit, and he was going to get his pistol and all that... The second night.
So we won the amateur prize, which was five dollars...
